title: Asthma predicted effector genes (Valette K et al. 2021)
bodyHtml:
This table displays results from the study:

Prioritization of candidate causal genes for asthma in susceptibility loci derived from UK Biobank.
Valette K et al.
Commun Biol. 2021 Jun 8;4(1):700. doi: 10.1038/s42003-021-02227-6.
PMID: 34103634

This study used multiple lines of evidence to prioritize potential effector genes for asthma. Starting with a GWAS for asthma associations in 56,167 asthma cases and 352,255 controls of European ancestry from UK Biobank, the following methods were applied to evaluate the genes at genetically associated loci:

  • A transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) was performed using the S-PrediXcan method (Barbeira et al., 2018). The GWAS summary statistics were integrated with an eQTL dataset from 1,038 human lung samples (Hao et al., 2012). "Yes" in the Lung TWAS column below indicates that the gene had transcriptome-wide significance (p < 2.51E−6) in the lung TWAS.
  • A colocalization analysis was performed using the COLOC package in R (Giambartolomei et al., 2014) to test whether asthma-associated SNPs were colocalized with blood eQTLs from the eQTLGen Consortium. "Yes" in the Blood eGene column below indicates that the posterior probability of shared eQTL and GWAS associations (PP4) was greater than 60%.
  • Hi-C chromatin conformation analysis was performed in the GM12878 lymphoblastoid B cell line to detect contacts between SNPs and genes. "Yes" in the Hi-C column below indicates that a SNP associated with asthma at genome-wide significance (p < 5.0E−8) or a SNP in LD with it (using a r2 threshold of 0.6 based on the 1000 Genomes EUR reference panel) is in contact with the gene.
  • The overall asthma association score for each gene was retrieved from the Open Targets resource; the Open Targets asthma score column displays the numerical score (ranging from 0 to 1).
  • Putative causal genes were compared with the list of druggable targets in the Drug-Gene Interaction Database (DGIdb). "Yes" in the Drug-gene Interaction Database (DGIdb) column indicates that the gene is listed as a druggable target in DGIdb.
  • Putative causal genes were compared with the list of druggable targets in the druggable genome study (Finan et al., 2017). "Yes" in the Druggable genome column indicates that the gene is present in the druggable genome list.
  • Putative causal genes were compared with a recently assembled list of asthma drug targets (El-Husseini et al., 2020). "Yes" in the Asthma drug target column indicates that the gene is present on the list.
